text: We have brought this inquiry, then, to an important point. In the article GOVERNMENT, we have seen that, unless the people hold in their own hands an official power of control to the act and of their governors the government will be inevitably vicicious. We have now seen that they cannot exercise the control to any beneficial pur- pises, without the means of forming a correct judgment upon the conduct of their representatives. We have likewise seen, that one of the names necessary to enable them to judge correctly of the conduct of their representatives, is the liberty to every body of publishing reports of what they do. It remains to inquire by what other acts like press to be made to contribute to the same desirable end.
